transcript:
Header: 2025-06-11 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (FinEdge CTO), Sara Kim (Head of ML Ops), Evan Li (Infra)

Summary: quick discovery for Dedicated capacity. FinEdge runs low-latency inference for risk scoring during market hours, needs isolation for customer PII and deterministic costs. They're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; leaning Dedicated with burst to hosted for spikes.

00:00:02 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — i'm maya, i'm the AE on this account. Liam is our solutions engineer. can each of you intro real quick?
00:00:12 Raj Patel: Sure, i'm raj, cto at finedge, we run a couple of real-time scoring pipelines for credit and fraud, some p ii in the features so isolation is important.
00:00:22 Sara Kim: Sara here, lead ml ops. we own model infra and deployment. we're particularly worried about tail latency and cost during market open.
00:00:31 Evan Li: Evan, infra eng. i'll be involved in network/VPC setup and the onboarding.
00:00:40 Liam O'Connor: Great, thanks. high level, we wanted to understand your throughput and latency SLOs, security constraints, and how you expect to scale over time.
00:00:52 Raj Patel: For latency, 99th perc needs to be under 120ms for our short prompt models, p99 for longer sessions we can tolerate 250-300ms. Throughput: baseline 200 qps during off-peak, peak 2k qps during market open windows, but bursts can be short and spiky.
00:01:12 Sara Kim: Also want dedicated hardware because we can't have PII hitting multi-tenant GPUs; auditability is required, SOC2 and logs for all requests, and KMS integration.
00:01:25 Maya Chen: Understood. on Redwood Dedicated you'd get reserved GPU pools, isolated tenancy for your workloads, and options for a private control plane if you need it. we also support KMS integrations and audit logs. would you consider host-level private deployment or is dedicated shared within our infra okay if logically isolated?
00:01:43 Raj Patel: Prefer isolated within your infra first, but if needed we can consider VPC/private deploy. cost delta matters though.
00:01:52 Liam O'Connor: Quick clarifying question on burst model: are you expecting long sustained bursts during day trading, or shorter spikes? and what's your tolerance for fallback to hosted shared capacity?
00:02:04 Evan Li: Mostly short spikes, like 5-10 minutes, but could be simultaneous across regions. fallback is okay but needs to be deterministic: we can't have sudden model swaps with different outputs for compliance.
00:02:19 Sara Kim: Also need version pinning and rollout controls. if we switch model weights during a spike it's fine only if it's the same model family and we have deterministic behavior or a pre-approved fallback.
00:02:33 Liam O'Connor: Got it. we have model pinning and rollout policies, canary and a/b style. for bursts we support configured burst capacity — you can reserve a baseline GPU pool and have a policy to burst to spare hosted capacity; we can also prioritize routing so sensitive calls always stay on reserved hardware and non-sensitive can burst.
00:02:52 Raj Patel: How do you ensure isolation? is it tenancy at the GPU node level or scheduler-level up to the tenant?
00:03:02 Liam O'Connor: it's a mix: on Dedicated you get reserved nodes allocated to your org. we do hypervisor/driver isolation and scheduling so that your containers/VMs run on dedicated GPU sets. networking can be VPC peered to your environment and we surface audit logs per request. if you need full air-gapped/on-prem, Private is an option but adds ops overhead.
00:03:25 Maya Chen: cost-wise dedicated is committed monthly or annual and gives you predictable unit costs; burst credits can be used but billed differently. i'll follow up with concrete tiered pricing.
00:03:36 Raj Patel: When you say burst to hosted, is the model identical? we need to avoid model drift or any parameter differences.
00:03:45 Liam O'Connor: Good point — we can pin model versions across variants. for hosted fallback we tend to use a compatible model variant (same weights) or a pre-agreed downgrade policy. we also provide checksum/versioning so you can validate.
00:04:02 Sara Kim: What about quantized variants? some of our workloads can use int8 to reduce latency but quality tests are strict.
00:04:11 Liam O'Connor: We recommend benchmark-driven quantization. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per model and workload. during a POC we'll run A/B comparisons and gather eval metrics.
00:04:24 Evan Li: Networking. we'd need SAML SSO for console, and we run KMS via our cloud provider HSM. can Redwood integrate?
00:04:33 Maya Chen: Yes, we support SAML and SSO and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping. we'll share the security whitepaper.
00:04:42 Raj Patel: Great. on scaling policies: can you describe autoscale granularity and cold-start behavior? we've seen slow cold starts when scaling up from zero.
00:04:53 Liam O'Connor: Dedicated pools are kept warm by default to hit latency SLOs. scaling can be based on qps, GPU utilization, or token throughput. warm scaling is faster because the KV cache and model artifacts are preloaded. cold start from zero is not recommended for strict latency SLAs.
00:05:10 Sara Kim: How about continuous batching and latency tradeoffs? we can't accept batching that increases p99 beyond our target.
00:05:18 Liam O'Connor: The runtime supports continuous batching with strict SLO-aware batching. you can set max-batch-ms and priority routing for low-latency flows, ensuring premium calls get immediate execution.
00:05:30 Raj Patel: Security question again: audit logs need to show token-level metadata and request IDs; how long are logs retained?
00:05:38 Maya Chen: Retention tiers are configurable; enterprise customers can request extended retention. we'll include audit log retention options in the docs.
00:05:45 Evan Li: Do you support private deployment in our VPC? we might need that for compliance if multi-tenant isn't allowed.
00:05:52 Liam O'Connor: Yes, Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem. it's a different engagement and licensing model; we can outline tradeoffs.
00:06:03 Raj Patel: Ok, technical deep dive notes: we run two major model families — one smaller 2B family for short prompts, and a 7B for contextual scoring. expected token lengths average 120 tokens for scoring. what's recommended GPU footprint?
00:06:18 Liam O'Connor: For 2B we typically recommend 1 GPU per ~150-200 qps baseline depending on batch settings; 7B you might need 1 GPU per ~60-100 qps. precise sizing we'll confirm with your sample payloads and token distributions.
00:06:33 Sara Kim: Are KV caches per-tenant? we want per-session caches to reduce token compute.
00:06:39 Liam O'Connor: KV caches are scoped per model deployment and can be cached per-tenant or shared depending on the architecture you choose. for privacy you'd opt for tenant-scoped caches.
00:06:50 Raj Patel: Any suggestions for controlling unit costs?
00:06:54 Maya Chen: Common levers: batching configs, prefix/KV caching, quantization, and routing certain low-sensitivity calls to cheaper model variants. Redwood Optimize can run suggestions after baseline measurements.
00:07:06 Evan Li: Do you have SLAs for latency and uptime on Dedicated?
00:07:10 Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated ships with SLA-backed uptime and we can include latency targets in the contract for critical routes. we'll propose options in the pricing doc.
00:07:18 Raj Patel: Okay, i want to see a benchmark with our traffic shape. what do you need from us?
00:07:23 Liam O'Connor: sample payloads, token distributions, QPS patterns over a trading day, and any model artifacts. we'll run local perf tests and then run against a dedicated pool in a POC.
00:07:35 Sara Kim: We'll also need to validate deterministic outputs across burst fallback and quantized variants.
00:07:41 Liam O'Connor: We'll add deterministic checksums and regression tests into the benchmark playbook.
00:07:48 Maya Chen: Recap and next steps: we'll send pricing/tiers and security docs by Thursday, Liam will share benchmark checklist and request sample traffic, and we'll schedule the perf run for late June.
00:07:59 Raj Patel: Sounds good. any blockers on your side?
00:08:03 Maya Chen: none. we'll follow up on the calendar invite and next actions.
00:08:08 Evan Li: thanks everyone.

Notes / artifacts mentioned: pricing tiers doc (will be shared), SOC2 whitepaper, benchmark playbook, sample payloads spreadsheet (customer to provide).

End of transcript.
